title: Proctologist visit
what: The doctor examines the anus and the rectum. The exam is short, and the doctor is gentle.
why: For blood in the stool, pain or itching in the anus, hemorrhoids, fissures, constipation, and for screening after age 40 to 50.
duration: the visit usually takes 15 to 30 minutes; conclusion right away
tell_doctor: What bothers you and for how long
Whether there was blood, and what color
How often you have a bowel movement and what it is like

prepare.title: Cleansing
prepare.text: You are often asked to empty your bowel before the visit, sometimes with an enema or mini-enema. Ask the clinic exactly how.

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: Take a shower in the morning. No special skin prep is needed.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually a light breakfast is fine.

bring: Colonoscopy or test results, if you have them
steps: The doctor asks about your complaints
You lie on your side with your knees drawn up, or kneel on all fours
The doctor looks at the skin around the anus
Gently checks the rectum with a gloved, gel-covered finger
Sometimes looks with a short tube called an anoscope
Explains what was found and prescribes treatment
feel: It feels awkward. That is normal, and for the doctor it is routine work
The finger exam can be unpleasant, but it is brief
With a fissure it can hurt. Tell the doctor
after: You can usually go about your day right after the exam
A little gel or traces of blood are possible, especially with a fissure
If needed, the doctor will send you for a colonoscopy
red_flags: Heavy bleeding from the anus, weakness or dizziness: call your local emergency number
Severe pain with swelling and fever: see a doctor urgently

faq.a: Usually not. It is just unpleasant. With a fissure, the doctor can numb the area with a gel.

faq.q: Is blood in the stool always hemorrhoids?
faq.a: Not always. That is why it is important to see a doctor and not treat yourself.

reminders.text: Proctologist visit tomorrow. Ask whether you need to empty your bowel in the morning, and how to do it.
